The clinical summary presents a classic, well-characterized presentation of acute unilateral peripheral vestibulopathy. The planned head-impulse test (with expected corrective saccade) further confirms a peripheral vestibular deficit — specifically of the horizontal semicircular canal afferent pathway — consistent with vestibular neuritis. While “vestibular neuritis” is often used interchangeably with “acute vestibular neuropathy”, the term reflects idiopathic, presumed inflammatory or post-infectious dysfunction of the superior vestibular nerve (which innervates the anterior and horizontal canals), typically sparing hearing and lower cranial nerve function — precisely matching this case.
